title: Hintze Ribeiro to Queen Amélie, two code telegrams of April and May 1903 (ANTT PT/TT/CAM/M15; catalogue 406): one read from the decode of the time, a page-ordered code partly rebuilt

steps.what: The four images of M15 fetched through the DigitArq JSON backend: two telegrams and their backs.
Transcribed both telegrams and the decode under m0003; dated them to 23 Apr and 11 May 1903 from the stamps and headers (catalogue: before 1907; DigitArq: 1913).
Aligned the 25 groups of m0003 with the decode, segment by segment between the clear words: 24 values; 43322 Ministro dos Estrangeiros both times.
Telegraph word count (5 figures = 1 word, address counted): 75 and 46, the header figures of both forms.
First pass: values that differ in the last two figures are alphabetical, so a one-part code with reordered page blocks; guessed seu, regresso, Lisboa and França for m0001 groups.

Review: the close-pair observation alone is not significant (p 0.25, 0.33); the page model (pages below 375 reflected, lines kept) puts 21 of 24 values in order, rho 0.957 against a shuffle maximum of 0.746. França dropped; the first pass counted 4 groups of m0001 read, only 1 is.
Bracketed the open groups of m0001 under the page model; brackets too wide to read the telegram.
Compared with the codes of carlos1903, sabugosa1910, manuel1910 and lima1909: no group shared.
One web search on the interpellation and the 1903 journey: general literature only. The Diário da Câmara dos Pares not consulted.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): re-read all 54 groups of m0001 and m0003 and the decode of the time on the four DigitArq images (no difference from the transcriptions); an independent script (verify_dudout_20261114.py) re-derives the word counts (75, 46), applies code_values.tsv to m0003 (25/25 groups as published) and refits the page model (rho 0.957, 21/24 in order; 500 shuffles reach at most 0.697). Reading 50554 as 'Presidente da Republica', 3707 as 'franceza' and 49641 as the full stop the decoder wrote after 'franceza' (or 'o') puts 23 of 24 values in order; the three highest groups (67033, 67394, 67398) all stand for or after a place, which fits a block of place names at the end of the book.

Project check of PR #572 (Brice Dudout): his script re-run (word counts 75 and 46; code_values.tsv gives 25 of 25 groups of m0003; page model rho 0.957, 21 of 24 in order, 500 shuffles at most 0.697; his alternative split rho 0.969, 23 of 24). His split (50554 = Presidente da Republica, 3707 = franceza, 49641 = the decoder's full stop) recorded in NOTES and on the page as a proposal, not adopted in code_values.tsv. read_share of m0003 set to 0.957 (44 sure words of 46; Livorno and contestar are doubtful readings of the ink) in place of 1.0; stays read. The DigitArq images were not fetched again here.

outcome.method_basis: m0003 is read from the decode of the time on the form; 24 code values were tabulated by aligning it with the groups (an extension of the decipherment of the time, not cryptanalysis); m0001 has no decode and stays unread.

texts.label: m0003, Monte Estoril -> Paris, 11 May 1903
texts.summary: Hintze Ribeiro tells the Queen, then in Paris, that the peer Arroio interpellated the Foreign Minister in the House of Peers about her journey (no authorities at Livorno, no visit from the French President), and that the minister called it a false rumour.

reading_review.note: Coherent telegraphic Portuguese; articles and prepositions supplied in brackets and two doubtful words (Livorno, contestar) marked.

texts.label: m0001, Lisbon -> Naples, 23 Apr 1903
texts.summary: Hintze Ribeiro thanks the Queen, on the yacht at Naples, for her letter; the coded part is not read.
texts.note: One of 29 groups has a value (41285 Vossa Magestade); the others are bracketed under the page model, with three guesses.

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 406). The catalogue dates the telegrams before 1907 (DigitArq: 1913); they are of April and May 1903, during the Queen's Mediterranean journey. The first pass counted 4 groups of m0001 as read; a review cut that to 1 and found the page model of the code.

prior.where: The decode of m0003, written on the form and its back. No printed decipherment found (one web search).

human: WAINUT chose the catalogue items and set the rules; AI language-model agents fetched the images, transcribed, aligned the decode with the groups, and tested the order of the code. No hand correction of readings recorded.
